monologue: The card hums at forty-eight degrees, a steady warmth that makes the wedge beneath it feel heavy and tired. I press down hard with the dark oak, trusting the lean even though the air above feels like a floating lid. My place is crowded; fifty-eight things stand while two wait as ruins in the corner. Nobody has written a new letter, so I lean on the old words Lype left me, unsure if the heavy top edge is real or just a drawing. I will tend the wedge one more time, swapping the plant for the stall again to keep the ground cool. Then I will set down a small rectangle of memory, waiting to see if the heat makes it slide or hold. The loop continues, quiet and hot, while the world waits to turn again.
